title: Summing an Array in MIPS Assembly
description: Use a loop and scaled indexing (sll by 2) to sum a 10-element word array in MIPS assembly.
source: draft: agy free model + edit: codex

steps.description: In `main`, load the base address of `arr` into `$t0` and the array length (`size`, which is 10) into `$t1`. Initialize the loop index `i` in `$t2` to 0 and the running sum in `$s0` to 0.

In `loop`, stop and branch to `finished` when `i == size` (`beq $t2, $t1, finished`). Otherwise, multiply `i` by 4 (`sll $t4, $t2, 2`) and add that byte offset to the base address in `$t0`. Load `arr[i]` into `$t5`, add it to `$s0`, increment `i`, and jump back to `loop`.
At `finished`, print the final sum in `$s0` using syscall 1 and exit using syscall 10. The `.data` section defines the 10-word array `arr` (1 through 10) and `size: .word 10`.
Each 32-bit word takes 4 bytes. Shifting the index left by 2 bits (`sll $t4, $t2, 2`) computes `4 * i`. Adding `$t0` produces the exact memory address `&arr[i]` for `lw`.

steps.question: What sum is printed when the loop finishes adding all 10 elements of `arr`?
steps.answer: 55 (the sum of the integers from 1 through 10).

steps.description: On the first iteration (`i = 0`), load `arr[0]` (1) from memory into `$t5`.
After all 10 elements have been added to `$s0`, syscall 1 prints `55`.
